quizzes.title: World Wetlands Day 2026: MCQ
quizzes.passage: World Wetlands Day draws attention to wetlands, which are places where land is covered by water. The day commemorates the Convention on Wetlands of International Importance, widely known as the Ramsar Convention, which was signed in 1971. The Convention has member states from across the world, and India is one of its signatories. India's wetlands are part of a group known as the Ramsar Network, and this network has been in the news. The Ramsar Network refers to India's wetlands that are recognised under the Convention. The day therefore connects a global treaty with sites inside India. Two wetlands in different states are also in the news. The Patna Bird Sanctuary is located in Uttar Pradesh and is a bird sanctuary of that state. The Chhari-Dhand Wetland Reserve is located in Gujarat and is known for a mysterious local phenomenon. Together, these two places show that wetlands in India range from bird habitats to reserves. Both sites are wetlands that have drawn attention for distinct reasons. The observance therefore gives attention to wetlands in general, as well as to specific sites that are being highlighted this year. The topic thus has three parts: the day itself, the Convention, and the sites in the news. The booklet presents this news in its Why in News section, which is the opening part of the topic.

questions.q: In which year was the Patna Bird Sanctuary established?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the Patna Bird Sanctuary was established in 1991.

questions.q: What is the designated theme for World Wetlands Day in 2026?
options: Wetlands and Climate Change: A Natural Solution
Wetlands and Traditional Knowledge: Celebrating Cultural Heritage
Wetlands for a Sustainable Urban Future
Wetlands and Biodiversity: Life in the Water
questions.explanation: The booklet gives the 2026 theme as Wetlands and Traditional Knowledge: Celebrating Cultural Heritage.

questions.q: Chir Batti night lights are seen across which grassland?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Chir Batti night lights of Chhari-Dhand are seen across the Banni Grasslands.

questions.q:
Read the assertion and reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion (A): India became a signatory to the Ramsar Convention on 1 February 1982.
Reason (R): The Convention came into force in 1975.
options: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
questions.explanation: Both statements are true in the booklet, but the year the Convention came into force does not explain India's signing date.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Patna Bird Sanctuary   ->   A. Etah District
II. Chhari-Dhand Wetland Reserve   ->   B. Rann of Kutch
III. Signing place of the Ramsar Convention   ->   C. Iran
IV. World Wetlands Day   ->   D. 2 February
questions.explanation: Patna is in Etah District, Chhari-Dhand is in the Rann of Kutch, the Convention was signed in Iran, and the day is observed on 2 February.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Convention is the only international treaty that addresses a specific ecosystem.
II. The Patna Bird Sanctuary is the largest bird sanctuary in its state.
III. The Convention was signed in 1975.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement I matches the booklet, since Patna is the state's smallest sanctuary and the Convention was signed in 1971.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
1. The Union Environment Minister added new wetlands to India's Ramsar Network.
2. The Patna Bird Sanctuary is located in Rajasthan.
3. World Wetlands Day is observed on 2 March.
questions.explanation: Only the first statement is correct, since the booklet places Patna in Uttar Pradesh and the day on 2 February.

questions.q: In which district of Uttar Pradesh is the Patna Bird Sanctuary located?

quizzes.title: Wetlands: Meaning and Classification MCQ
quizzes.passage: The February 2026 current affairs booklet, in its environment and biodiversity section, places its discussion of wetlands after the coverage of World Wetlands Day. The wetland section opens with a definition. According to the booklet, a wetland is a place in which land is covered by water. This definition is applied to a wide range of water bodies rather than to a single type of habitat. The booklet's examples include rivers, swamps and wet grasslands. Peatlands are also named, and so are mangroves. Each of these examples is treated as a kind of wetland under the definition. After the definition, the booklet turns to the way wetlands are arranged into groups for classification. The classification is presented as a separate step, so the section moves from a definition to a grouping. The Ramsar Convention coverage follows this part of the booklet, and that coverage is set out in its own section. Readers of the booklet will therefore find the definition, the examples, and the classification in one connected discussion, in that order. The definition in the booklet is short, and it uses the words land and water to describe the place. Each example in the list is named in the booklet and is not described further in the wetland section.

questions.q: How many segments are wetlands classified into?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that wetlands are classified into three segments.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed among the water bodies included in the wetland definition?
questions.explanation: The booklet's list includes peatlands, mangroves and rivers, but not glaciers.

questions.q:
Read the assertion and reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion (A): The water cover of a wetland may be seasonal or permanent.
Reason (R): All wetlands are covered by salt water.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet says the water cover may be seasonal or permanent, but it does not say all wetlands are covered by salt water.

questions.q: Which of the following is included in the wetland definition along with other coastal areas?
questions.explanation: The booklet includes coral reefs together with other coastal areas in the wetland definition.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Wetlands may hold water that is salt, fresh or in between.
II. Every wetland must have permanent water cover.
III. Tidal flats are included in the wetland definition.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while statement II is wrong because the water cover may be seasonal.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
1. Lakes are included in the wetland definition.
2. Mangroves are classified as a separate segment of wetlands.
3. Deltas are included in the wetland definition.
questions.explanation: Lakes and deltas are listed as wetlands, but mangroves are only named as an example and not as a separate segment.

questions.q: Which underground feature is included in the booklet's list of wetland water bodies?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists underground aquifers among the water bodies included in the wetland definition.

quizzes.title: Wetlands: Meaning and Classification TITA
quizzes.passage: The February 2026 current affairs booklet treats wetlands in its environment and biodiversity section, and the discussion opens with what a wetland is. The booklet describes a wetland as a place where land is covered by water. The term applies to lakes and rivers, and it also applies to swamps, wet grasslands and peatlands. Its reach therefore extends across many kinds of water bodies. The booklet then moves on from this definition to the way wetlands are arranged into groups for classification. Each group is described in the booklet by name, and the names are used to sort the wetlands discussed earlier. Readers of this section will see the definition first and the classification after it. The discussion of the Ramsar Convention follows, in a separate part of the booklet, and it is not part of the wetland definition. The section therefore runs from a broad description of land covered by water to a more specific system of groups. The booklet presents the definition simply, so the key words are land, water and cover. The booklet's wording on wetlands is short and direct, and it does not add examples beyond those it lists. This section of the booklet is short and set out in plain language.

questions.q: Into how many segments are wetlands classified? (give the number)
questions.explanation: The booklet says wetlands are classified into three segments.

questions.q: Name the third segment into which wetlands are classified. (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet's three segments are Inland, Coastal and Human-made wetlands.

questions.q: Which underground water body is included in the booklet's wetland definition? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists underground aquifers among the water bodies included in the wetland definition.

questions.q: Which feature is listed in the booklet alongside deltas and mangroves? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet's list places tidal flats next to deltas and mangroves.

questions.q: Which feature is included along with other coastal areas? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet includes coral reefs together with other coastal areas.

questions.q: The booklet says the water cover of a wetland may be seasonal or what? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the water cover of a wetland may be seasonal or permanent.

questions.q: The booklet says wetland water may be salt, fresh or what? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet says wetland water may be salt, fresh or somewhere in between.
